text: Microsoft 365 Copilot can help you get more value from meetings, both while they're happening and after they've ended. During a meeting, Copilot can follow the live discussion, help you catch up and suggest useful questions to ask. Afterward, it can help you review decisions, identify action items, and turn the discussion into something actionable. Let's look at how to set it up and use it. In Microsoft Teams, I open my calendar, select a meeting, and go to Options, then Copilot and other AI. Under Allow Copilot and Facilitator, there are two main options. Only during the meeting, let's Copilot follow the live discussion without saving a transcript, but someone needs to activate it. During and after the meeting requires transcription, so Copilot can work with the spoken discussion after the meeting ends. Here, the second option is already configured by my organization's administrator. Keep in mind that the available settings depend on your Microsoft 365 license and your organization's policies. Now, I've joined the Teams meeting. First, I select More Actions, then Record and Transcribe, and Start Transcription. Next, I select the Copilot icon from the meeting controls to open the side panel. Copilot isn't limited to what's written in the meeting chat. It can also follow the live spoken conversation. Let's say I've joined the meeting a few minutes late. I can ask, what have I missed so far? Summarize the key discussion points and decisions. Copilot gives me a summary based on the discussion it has access to, starting from when Copilot Processing or Transcription began. I can also use it as a thinking partner. For example, what are the main points of disagreement and what question should I ask before we make a decision? Copilot helps identify different perspectives and suggests questions worth considering. These conversations with Copilot are private to me. Other participants won't see my questions or its responses, although they may still be subject to organizational compliance policies. Now, let's look at what happens after the meeting ends. I open the completed meeting in Microsoft Teams and select the Recap tab. Depending on my license and meeting settings, I can review AI-generated notes, key discussion points, suggested tasks, and the transcript. Instead of reviewing the entire recording, I can quickly understand what happened and what needs follow-up. But before relying on the Recap, I want to verify the important details. So I open the transcript section and check critical decisions, owners, and deadlines against what was actually said. Depending on my permissions, I can also download the transcript as a Word or VTT file. Now, let's take this one step further. A meeting Recap is useful, but I often need to turn that information into something I can share with leadership. So I open Copilot from the completed meeting and enter this prompt. Create a one-page executive summary from this meeting. Include the objective, key discussion points, decisions made, action items with owners and due dates, unresolved risks, and recommended next steps. Keep it concise, flag anything unconfirmed, and don't invent missing details. I submit the prompt, and Copilot generates a structured executive summary based on the available meeting information. Now I have a draft I can review, refine, and share. I could also ask Copilot to draft a follow-up email or prepare the agenda for the next meeting. The key is to verify the output before treating it as an agreed record. Remember, Copilot's meeting capabilities depend on your license, permissions, and organizational settings. During a meeting, it can work with live spoken discussions without saving a transcript, depending on the configuration. After a meeting, it generally needs an accessible saved transcript to work with the spoken conversation. And as always, verify critical facts, decisions, and commitments before acting on AI-generated outputs. Follow your organization's policies when transcribing meetings, handling sensitive information, and sharing meeting content. The goal is to let Copilot handle more of the administrative work, so you can focus on the conversation, the decisions, and what happens next.
